text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert INC-20260314-78 triggered for service=runtime-canary; symptom=5xx spike, latency p95 up 3x. Alert rule: canary-error-rate > 5% over 2m. Runbook: #runbooks/canary-failure.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident INC-20260314-78 created and paging escalation policy 'runtime-oncall'. Notified: maya.

maya: On it, acked in PD. Starting triage. Is this only canary or rolling to prod?

alex: I launched the canary 4m ago with release v2026.3. The rollout target was 10% traffic to canary. I see rollback option ready.

sam: I can take logs. Preliminary metrics: canary 5xx rate 12% last 3m, prod stable ~0.4%. Sounds like release regression.

rio: paging in #eng-runtime and adding @alex @sam for visibility.

maya: Thanks. sam attach logs from the canary pod group and any stack traces. Also verify whether autoscaler flapped.

sam: Logs:```
2026-03-14T15:01:22Z [runtime] ERROR handler.cpp:142 request_id=abcd1234 status=502 upstream=kv_fetch timeout_ms=1200
2026-03-14T15:01:23Z [runtime] WARN kv_cache.cpp:87 evicted key=seq_4096
2026-03-14T15:02:05Z [runtime] ERROR attention_kernel.cu: invalid memory access
```

alex: seeing similar in local repro. Looks like attention kernel assertion after quant path enabled. I pushed a build that toggles quant-mode off for canary but the rollout might need to be reverted.

karen: Any customer impact yet? SLO dashboards show user-facing 5xx spike for the canary cohort, but some traffic shaping routes may have sent a bit to prod. I'm pulling top customer traces; will report in 2m.

pagerduty: INC-20260314-78 currently acknowledged by maya (oncall). Escalation suspended.

maya: Triage conclusion: new runtime change in v2026.3 triggers rare kernel failure on quantized models. Impact limited to canary, but we see ~8% of total fronted requests routed to canary (config drift). Risk of more. Plan: disable canary traffic (set rollout to 0%), then redeploy canary with quant-mode disabled, or rollback to v2026.2. Thoughts?

alex: Quickest is to cut canary traffic to 0 and roll back the canary service to v2026.2. I can revert the rollout and trigger helm rollback.

sam: To cut traffic:```
kubectl patch canary runtime-canary -p '{"spec":{"traffic":0}}' --type=merge
# then: helm rollback runtime-canary 1
```

rio: I'll run the patch. Running now.

rio: patch applied. traffic->0. Observability: canary request volume dropping to near zero.

karen: Confirming customer traces: AcmeCorp and BetaApps saw errors routed via a proxy path that touched canary. AcmeCorp error rate peaked at 15% for a 2m window. Support impact: we're opening a ticket for AcmeCorp customers impacted between 15:01-15:04 UTC.

maya: Good. Next step rollback helm. alex, you can run rollback and I'll monitor. If rollback fails, we abort and cut traffic entirely and restart nodes.

alex: Rolling back now. helm rollback runtime-canary 1 --namespace inference || echo rollback-failed
deploy-bot: Deploy job started for runtime-canary rollback to v2026.2 (job id jb-5589). Logs: pulling image, applying manifests.

sam: Watching logs: new pods coming up, health checks green. No attention kernel errors in new pods so far.

maya: Observability: 5xx rate across cluster returning to baseline within 60s. p95 latency also normalizing.

karen: Notified CSM for AcmeCorp with initial impact window and apology. Support assigned ticket INC-20260314-78-A.

pagerduty: Incident INC-20260314-78 status: acknowledged -> in_progress. Assigned: maya, alex.

alex: rollback complete. runtime-canary now at v2026.2 and traffic 0. I disabled the problematic quant flag in CI for future builds.

sam: Post-rollback metrics: canary 5xx -> 0.3%, prod steady. No further errors in logs.

maya: Great. I'm going to de-escalate PD if we keep stable for 10m. Leave incident open for postmortem action items.

incident-bot: Incident timeline note appended: root cause likely quantization flag + new attention kernel change in v2026.3. Affected: canary only (mis-configured rollout). Mitigation: traffic cut and rollback to v2026.2. 

karen: Action items: 1) patch rollout guard to enforce max canary traffic to 10% (rio). 2) add automated quant-mode test in canary CI (alex). 3) update runbook with rollback commands and PD routing (maya). 4) reach out to AcmeCorp support contact with RCA when ready (karen).

rio: I'll take item 1, starting a PR for guardrails.

alex: I'll add a CI integration test that spins up a small FP/quant matrix against the attention kernel.

maya: I'll create the incident postmortem doc and link PD timeline. Please add any logs or repro steps to the doc. Target: postmortem draft in 48h.

pagerduty: INC-20260314-78 marked as mitigated in PagerDuty.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: runtime-canary canary failure. Resolution note: rollback + traffic cut. Please run postmortem template: #templates/incident-postmortem.

karen: Thanks team. Quick wins: customer notified, rollback done. Will follow up with support ticket details. :thumbsup:

maya: Closing conversation here, will update when postmortem is ready.

alex: Good catch everyone.

sam: Nice coordination.

rio: PR opened for rollout guard: draft link posted in #eng-runtime.

incident-bot: Thread auto-archived in 72h per channel policy.
